title: The box law at every power of two
claim: Obstructed under the frozen criterion: C1 (at every n = 2^m >= 4 the box's corner series is 1/(1 + L(w^4))) is not proved for every m; it is proved at each power of two from 4 to 512 by exact computation (agreement on 2n(n - 1) + 4n terms, as many as the sum of the orders of the two linear recurrences). Proved (refereed): Theorem 7, the box's corner series is R(w^2), R(s) the (L, 0) entry of the inverse of the block operator K_n = I - [[sD + S_LL, S_LR], [S_RL, sD^T + S_RR]] on the rows of the two end columns, S_XY = sum_h N_XY(h) s^h (I - sP)^-(h-1); Proposition 8, at n = 2^m over GF(2) the row path is nilpotent, det(I + xP_(n-2)) = C_(m-1)(x^2), det(I + xP_(n-3)) = C_(m-2)(x^4), so the blocks are explicit and C1 at n is one finite identity; Proposition 9, det(I + zP_n^o) = 1 + L(z) for the looped path, so C1 says the corner returns, every four steps, as the loop end of a looped path of n sites. Corollary 10, the same decomposition counts the walks to any inner target, so the count of REACH-HALVES-20261110-001A (B137) is a sum over the corner's row of K_n^-1. Computed: C2 from 4 to 8 up to 256 to 512 (and its failures at 2, 3, 5, 6), C3 (first deviation from the quadrant at 8n) at 3 to 128, the four-corner formula at 4 to 128, the corner orbit's period 2^(floor(m/2)+1)(2n - 1) at 4 to 128; the looped path is a quotient of the corner's A^4-orbit wherever C1 holds, not an invariant subspace.
failure_conditions: A power of two n >= 4 at which the box's corner return series is not 1/(1 + L(w^4)) (computed false at 4 to 128).
A power of two n >= 4 at which 1/r_2n(w) != 1/r_n(w^2) + w^4 (computed false from 4 to 128).
remaining_obligations: the identity [K_n^-1]_00 = 1/(1 + L(s^2)) of Proposition 8 for every m
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38), its walk over GF(2), and the same walk with one or both far walls removed. Returns are a contact-level reading, so they do not depend on how the rings are declared beyond which contacts each ring holds (A45).
